# 1 Samuel Chapter 24 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164v–165r | **Source Image:** 1SA_024_page_001.jpg, 1SA_024_page_002.jpg

---

**24:1** And-it-was when-Saul returned from-after [the]-Philistines, and-they-told-him, saying, "Behold, David [is] in-[the]-wilderness of-En-gedi."

**24:2** And-took Saul three-thousand chosen men from-all Israel, and-went to-seek David and-his-men upon-[the]-face of-[the]-rocks of-[the]-wild-goats.

**24:3** And-he-came to-[the]-sheepfolds of-the-flock upon the-way, and-there [was]-a-cave, and-Saul went-in to-cover his-feet [le-hasekh et raglav]. And-David and-his-men [were]-sitting in-[the]-innermost-parts of-the-cave.

**24:4** And-said [the]-men of-David to-him, "Behold, the-day of-which YHWH said to-you, 'Behold, I [am]-giving your-enemy into-your-hand, and-you-shall-do to-him as-is-good in-your-eyes.'" And-arose David and-cut the-corner [kanaf] of-the-robe which [was]-to-Saul — secretly.

**24:5** And-it-was afterward, and-struck the-heart of-David him, because he-had-cut the-corner which [was]-to-Saul.

**24:6** And-he-said to-his-men, "Far-be-it for-me from-YHWH if I-should-do this thing to-my-lord, to-[the]-anointed of-YHWH [meshiach YHWH], to-stretch-out my-hand against-him, for [the]-anointed of-YHWH he [is]."

**24:7** And-David restrained [va-yeshassa'] his-men with-[these]-words and-did-not permit-them to-rise against-Saul. And-Saul arose from-the-cave and-went on-[the]-way.

**24:8** And-arose David after-this and-went-out from-the-cave and-called after Saul, saying, "My-lord the-king!" And-looked Saul behind-him, and-bowed David [with]-his-face to-the-ground and-prostrated-himself.

**24:9** And-said David to-Saul, "Why do-you-listen to-[the]-words of-a-man, saying, 'Behold, David seeks your-harm'?

**24:10** Behold, this day your-eyes have-seen that YHWH gave-you today into-my-hand in-the-cave, and-[someone]-said to-kill-you, but-I-spared-you [va-tachas]. And-I-said, 'I-will-not stretch-out my-hand against-my-lord, for [the]-anointed of-YHWH he [is].'

**24:11** And-my-father, see, indeed see the-corner of-your-robe in-my-hand, for when-I-cut the-corner of-your-robe, I-did-not kill-you. Know and-see that there-is-not in-my-hand evil or-rebellion, and-I-have-not sinned against-you, and-you [are]-hunting my-soul to-take-it.

**24:12** May-YHWH judge between-me and-between-you, and-may-YHWH avenge-me from-you, but-my-hand shall-not be against-you.

**24:13** As-says the-proverb [mashal] of-the-ancients, 'From-the-wicked goes-out wickedness,' but-my-hand shall-not be against-you.

**24:14** After whom has-the-king of-Israel gone-out? After whom are-you-pursuing? After a-dead dog, after a-single flea?

**24:15** And-YHWH shall-be [as]-judge, and-He-shall-judge between-me and-between-you, and-He-shall-see and-plead my-cause and-deliver-me from-your-hand."

**24:16** And-it-was when-David-finished speaking these words to-Saul, and-said Saul, "Is-this your-voice, my-son David?" And-Saul lifted-up his-voice and-wept.

**24:17** And-he-said to-David, "You [are]-more-righteous than-I, for you have-repaid-me the-good, and-I have-repaid-you the-evil.

**24:18** And-you have-declared today that you-have-done good with-me, in-that YHWH delivered-me into-your-hand and-you-did-not kill-me.

**24:19** For if a-man finds his-enemy, will-he-send-him-away on-[a]-good way? And-YHWH shall-repay-you good in-place-of this day which you-have-done for-me.

**24:20** And-now, behold, I-know that you-will-surely reign, and-the-kingdom of-Israel shall-be-established in-your-hand.

**24:21** And-now swear to-me by-YHWH that you-will-not cut-off my-seed after-me and-that you-will-not destroy my-name from-[the]-house of-my-father."

**24:22** And-swore David to-Saul. And-went Saul to-his-house, and-David and-his-men went-up to-the-stronghold.

**24:23** [This is 24:1 in English Bibles; the Hebrew verse numbering is one ahead throughout this chapter.]

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **24:3 — "to cover his feet"** (לְהָסֵךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו): A euphemism for relieving himself. The literal Hebrew preserves the idiom.

2. **24:4 — kanaf**: "Corner/wing" of the robe — symbolically, David has seized the royal authority (the robe's hem signifies status) but refuses to strike the person.

3. **24:5 — "his heart struck him"**: David's conscience convicts him for even this symbolic act against the LORD's anointed. This interior moral sensitivity distinguishes David from Saul.

4. **24:6 — meshiach YHWH**: "Anointed of YHWH" — the key theological concept. David refuses to harm God's chosen king, even when provoked and given opportunity. This principle governs chs. 24 and 26.

5. **24:14 — "dead dog... single flea"**: Self-deprecating metaphors emphasizing David's insignificance. The "dead dog" appears again in 2 Sam 9:8.

— EMET
